sg.vl: Front-center pays off at this small house
sg.ra: The O'Neill orchestra is unusually shallow for a Broadway house (668 seats across 19 rows A-T), so even mid-orch stays close; a TripAdvisor veteran calls it 'much smaller than it appears on the seating plan' — but rows A-D center are where Book of Mormon's verbal/facial comedy lands, and the mezzanine overhang at row L (per Headout/ticketiq) cuts off the rear, making front-center the unambiguous pick here rather than a splurge.

sg.vl: Value play if you accept the overhang cutoff
sg.ra: The O'Neill is a 1,066-seat house and the orchestra is only 19 rows deep, so 'rear' here is still closer than most Broadway mid-orchestras — Tickadoo explicitly names N-P as the value sweet spot. The tradeoff is the mezzanine overhang that Headout/TicketIQ place at row L, meaning anything from L back loses the top of the proscenium; for Book of Mormon's largely grounded staging this rarely costs you a gag, which is why multiple guides endorse it as the budget pick rather than writing it off as a skip.

sg.vl: The choreography view at the O'Neill
sg.ra: The O'Neill's front mezz is only 4 rows (A-D per Headout) and sits on a steep rake that Tickadoo calls the reason sightlines stay clear; Row A in particular gets repeatedly named as the best perch for Book of Mormon's 'Turn It Off' / 'Hasa Diga Eebowai' production numbers where you want the full formation, not just faces. This is a Jujamcyn-scale house (1,066) so 'front mezz' is genuinely close — not a Gershwin-style compromise.

The rear mezz at the O'Neill is the specific section where TickPick flags rows J-K-L (side rear mezz) as 'Restricted Legroom' — 'similar to airplane seats,' the cheapest tickets in the house and recently re-classified. Rate Your Seats calls sightlines 'most distant in the rear of the Mezzanine'; a documented AVFMS review from Mezz R row K reads 'Far back, no legroom.' Unlike front mezz the rake doesn't fully rescue you back here, and the E-row rail reported by SeatPlan eats into knees on L/R sides.
